answer_1.quote: We conduct experiments on four widely used translation tasks: CWMT17 Chinese-to-English (Zh→En), ASPEC Japanese-to-English (Ja→En), WMT14 French-to-English (Fr→En) and WMT14 English-to-German (En→De).
answer_1.outputs: generated target translation Y and its self‑estimated competency score Q_{X→Y}

answer_2.quote: We use BLEU to validate translation performance. As for self‑estimation, it considers whether an MT model is aware of its own competency... we evaluate the Pearson correlations between the self‑estimation scores and human judgments and compare against metrics such as SentBLEU, BERTScore, BLEURT, COMET, COMET‑QE, RTT‑SentBLEU, RTT‑BERTScore, Translation Probability (TP) and Monte Carlo Dropout Translation Probability (D‑TP).

answer_4.quote: We randomly select 200 sentences for each test set and translate them into the target language using CANMT models. Each sentence is scored by three professional translators presented with pairs of a source sentence and a translated hypothesis, following the scoring criteria ranging from 1 to 5 (larger is better). The human evaluation of translation quality mainly focuses on two aspects: accuracy and fluency.
answer_4.guideline: Professional translators rate each translation on a 1‑5 scale, assessing accuracy and fluency.
